---
title: "Releases"
---

The data is never committed to the repository: the five collections live in
five GitHub releases, all of them published (seven tags, since a release holds
at most 1,000 assets and `scjn-reglamentos` and `scjn-tratados` continue in a
`-2`).

| Collection | Release | Content | Keyed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| laws | `scjn-leyes` | 315 federal laws, 3,709 snapshots | `abrev` (the slug) |
| regulations | `scjn-reglamentos` | federal *reglamentos*: 1,087 instruments, 1,083 with text | `id_ordenamiento` |
| guidelines | `scjn-lineamientos` | federal *lineamientos*: 163 instruments, 126 with text | `id_ordenamiento` |
| treaties | `scjn-tratados` | international treaties: 1,455 instruments, 1,373 with text | `id_ordenamiento` |
| bylaws | `scjn-estatutos` | federal *estatutos* (the SCJN's category `ESTATUTO`): 379 instruments, 377 with text, 1,139 snapshots | `id_ordenamiento` |

(Counts as published on 2026-11-17.) The first column is the name the
collection has at the [command line](cli.qmd). Two bylaws are indexed with no or
incomplete snapshots because the SCJN serves one of their reforms with a
missing block that the completeness guard refuses: `178398` has none and
`111330` has 4 of its 5 reforms.

## The collections

The collections follow the SCJN's own documentary classification, not a
scheme of legal hierarchy or normative authority. The SCJN's search service
cannot list what its database holds (an empty query answers nothing), so each
collection was found in its own way. In every case an instrument is resolved
by the stable identifier the SCJN assigns to it (`id_ordenamiento`), never by
its rank in the search results.

- **Laws.** The federal laws, codes and the Constitution. The original list of
  the 315 laws was seeded from the catalogue of federal legislation that the
  Chamber of Deputies publishes; each law was then resolved by the SCJN's
  identifier and its whole table of reforms was crawled. Every text comes from
  the SCJN, and a law added since is discovered from the SCJN alone.
- **Regulations.** The federal instruments the SCJN classifies `REGLAMENTO`,
  found through unions of phrase searches for the federal scope (*ámbito*) and
  that category, with every page of results read to its end.
- **Guidelines.** The federal instruments the SCJN classifies `LINEAMIENTOS`,
  found the same way. Guidelines are administrative instruments, typically
  issued as *acuerdos*, whose provisions are numbered with ordinals rather than
  as articles; they may differ in issuing authority and legal effects.
- **Treaties.** Found through the scope under which the SCJN files them,
  `TRATADOS INTERNACIONALES`, whatever their category, since a treaty may be
  filed as a convention, an agreement or a protocol.
- **Bylaws.** The federal instruments the SCJN classifies `ESTATUTO`: the
  governing instruments of federal bodies, agencies and universities, found
  the same way as the regulations.

The SCJN reissues a regulation under a new identifier instead of reforming it,
so the regulations and the guidelines hold several instruments with the same
name. The releases ship all of them; choosing among them is the caller's
decision.

## Snapshots and what "current" means

A snapshot is a dated version of an instrument: its text as it read after one
reform. Every snapshot starts with a provenance header that always carries
`fuente: scjn`, `ordenamiento` (the instrument's name), `fecha_publicacion`
(the date the reform was published), `id_ordenamiento` (the identifier the
SCJN assigns to the instrument) and `reforma_id` (the reform the snapshot
reflects), and, when the SCJN gives them, `fecha_expedicion`, `categoria`,
`seccion_publicacion` and `materia`.

Current means the latest text the SCJN serves for an instrument at the time it
was collected; it is not a determination that every provision is in force.
Entry-into-force rules and judicial decisions may affect that. The SCJN's own
`vigencia` field is published as the SCJN gives it and is a different thing.

Each release carries an index plus one tarball per instrument. In `scjn-leyes`
each tarball's `estado.json` has the law's `actualizado`, the date of the newest
reform the SCJN serves for it (`actualizado_scjn`, or the date of the law's
newest snapshot when that is absent), never a DOF date. An instrument for which the SCJN serves no text belongs to its collection, is indexed with `snapshots: 0` and has no tarball;
reading it raises `SinTextoEnSCJN`.

## What an index carries

Per instrument, the index records the SCJN's own `nombre`, the tarball (`asset`) and
the number of `snapshots`, plus the SCJN's classification, one value per
instrument rather than per reform: `materia`, `vigencia`, `resumen` and, since
version 0.5.2, `categoria_ordenamiento` (`LEY`, `CODIGO`, `REGLAMENTO`, ...),
`ambito` (`FEDERAL`, `ESTATAL`, `TRATADOS INTERNACIONALES`), `pais` (the field that
tells the treaties apart) and, for a state-level instrument, `estado` and
`municipio`. A field the SCJN gives no value for is absent from the index, and the
readers return `None` for it; an index older than a field has no key for it
(every published index carries the classification wherever the SCJN gives it). The classification is not in a snapshot's provenance header.

## A release is a series

A GitHub release holds at most 1,000 assets, so a release is a series of tags:
a part keeps the bare tag (`scjn-tratados`) and a continuation adds `-<n>`
(`scjn-tratados-2`, `-3`, ...). The reader asks GitHub for the bare tag and then
probes `-1`, `-2`, ... until one answers 404.

## Where the releases live

The releases live in this repository,
[`legistlan/scjn`](https://github.com/legistlan/scjn/releases), and that is the
repository `scjn.release.release_repository()` names by default.
Set the environment variable `SCJN_RELEASE_REPOSITORY` (`<owner>/<name>`) to
point every lookup at a mirror of the releases elsewhere; it is read on every
call, so one process can be pointed elsewhere without reloading anything. The `gh` commands
that the packaging scripts print in `PUBLICAR.md` follow the same variable.

## Nothing is published automatically

No workflow publishes SCJN-derived data. The SCJN's search can return a
completely wrong document for an instrument, so a human decides what is safe to
publish. Every packaging script writes a `PUBLICAR.md` and uploads nothing; a
regenerated release is replaced in place (same tag, `--clobber`). See
[Crawl](crawl.qmd).

## Reading a release

[Command line](cli.qmd) puts a release on disk, and [Python](python.qmd) reads
it. Every reader is disk-first: it reads the cache and raises `AssetNotCached`
for anything not there.
